description: Plan step R3b (graph node rules). checkCall (the library entry shared by the command line, repository scripts and the loop board), the read side of the heartbeat files, the command line, the metrics event exit. Depends on FEAT-004.
steps: Read rules design sec 9.4 (checkCall, flags --signal/--role/--model/--session/--stage/--glm-spend/--peak-until/--waited-ms, exit codes 0/4/5/2, how a signal value is chosen from heartbeat or caller), sec 10.5 (rules.check event fields), sec 12 and sec 15 R3 (checkCall and command-line cases, listed in detail there). Read impl-plan Interpretations 12.

Write specs first: tests/rules-check.spec.ts and tests/rules-metrics.spec.ts. Every case in sec 15 R3 'checkCall and command line' that does not need a script to run: a queue rule on 'glm-peak is true' with a heartbeat sample within 45 s -> exit 5 with signals naming source heartbeat and the pid; same sample older than 45 s -> signal unreadable, exit 0, reason says no live host; two live heartbeats where the newer cannot read -> use the one that has a value; nextChangeAt in the past -> inverted; --signal glm-peak=true without heartbeat -> exit 5, source caller; --signal glm-peak=false overrides a true heartbeat; --signal code-freeze=true and --signal foo=1 -> usage error exit 2 with different stderr texts; glm-peak=yes -> exit 2; subjects rule: without --role no match with the reason in subjects, with --role subagent exit 4; stage rule with and without --stage; the gate and checkCall give the same verdict and the same text for the same rules and signals (block text identical, queue text differs only by the two sentences sec 9.4 names); peak stop level with --glm-spend necessary -> exit 5, reduce with optional -> exit 5, reduce with necessary -> exit 0; zeroed snapshot -> judged from an in-memory replay, notes say so, no byte of the rules directory changes (compare before/after listing and contents); missing state directory -> judged as empty state; project that never chose a level: --signal glm-peak=true --glm-spend optional -> exit 5 with the reduce/default text (contains builtin:glm-peak-reduce and 'the default; the human can change it'; 'until 18:00' / 'after 18:00' with --peak-until, 'now' / 'after peak ends' without); person-chosen stop -> text 'Peak mode set by the human at <local time>: stop' and builtin:glm-peak-stop; exactly one rules.check event per call with effect, exitCode, rules, peakMode.level/origin, glmSpend, glmPeakSource, unknownSignals, waitedMs, caller and no command text; the CLI's caller is 'cli'; an emitMetric exit that throws changes neither verdict nor text and leaves the rules directory untouched; negative --waited-ms and --peak-until without glm-peak are usage errors. Rules with a script action are reported in notes as not approved and judged by onError (no process is ever started: src/rules/ must not import node:child_process).

Implement src/rules/check.ts (checkCall using judgeInput/judge from FEAT-002, reading state without writing), src/rules/heartbeat.ts (liveHeartbeats: read-only parse of the heartbeat directory files, 45 s liveness; the writer arrives in FEAT-007), src/rules/cli.ts and scripts/rules/cli.mjs (subcommands show and check; separate process), src/rules/metrics.ts (emitMetric with an injectable exit, default does nothing; no import of any metrics module that does not exist), package.json script `rules`, and a new command-line section in docs/DEVELOPMENT.md. rules show prints what rules_show will print later (use one shared formatter now so FEAT-006 reuses it).
Commit once: 'feat(rules): checkCall and the rules command line (rules)' with gate results.

What exists now (for FEAT-006 and later):
- heartbeat.ts: HostHeartbeat (design shape; strict parse: host, at, sessions, runner, computed.glmPeak and catalog required, detectors optional, a nextChangeAt that is not a time is dropped), HEARTBEAT_FRESH_MS (plan.ts now imports it), readHeartbeats(paths) -> {heartbeats, unreadable} (reads .llm/rules/hosts/*.json, skips *.tmp, throws only when the directory cannot be listed), liveHeartbeats(list, nowMs) (45 s or less, newest first), hostPeak(live, nowMs). FEAT-007's writer must write the full shape, or readers list its file as unreadable in notes.
- check.ts: checkCall, showProject, RulesCheckError, HOST_SIGNALS, CheckOptions (adds metrics?: MetricExit, not in the design), CheckResult. The rule table is person rules sorted by id, then builtinRulesFor(level): the gate must build the same table in this order, and take command, writes and the first sentence from describeCall.
- call.ts describeCall(tool, args) -> {command?, writes?, attempt}. writes = file-tool targets (write, edit, str_replace_editor except view) plus redirect targets found by the guard's shellWrites; a shell write without a visible target (Set-Content and the like) has none. rules:files-only (FEAT-006) needs its own resolution against the session workspace.
- denial.ts denialText({attempt, effect, rules: [{hit, rule}], ticket?, peak}) is the shared refusal text for block and queue (renderCorrection). The gate passes ticket; no ticket is the checkCall form. Also exports conditionPhrase, setByPhrase, modeSentence, localMinute, localClock, builtinDeferral. Not built, for FEAT-006 and FEAT-008: the subagent right-path variant, the nested (run_code) variant, the stop and dispatch texts with the goal-paused sentence, the script block and queue texts that name the script path, the main agent's peak line.
- show.ts showText(ShowInput): peak mode line, GLM peak line, rules in force, waiting calls, signals, notes. FEAT-006's rules_show should call it after choosing the rules that apply to the calling session (showText does no role/model/session filtering) and may add the peakHours.en parenthetical and the peak line from the pricing service.
- metrics.ts emitMetric(event, project, exit?) never rejects; RulesCheckEvent is the only event; the exit is injected through CheckOptions.metrics (default nothing).
- cli.ts runCli(argv, {cwd, metrics?, now?}) -> {exitCode, stdout, stderr}; scripts/rules/cli.mjs; package.json script rules. show prints {ok, project, text, peakMode, signals, notes}.
- judge.ts exports ended(rule, input); signals.ts SignalReading has optional host; tests/rules-helpers.ts writeHeartbeat(paths, host, at, fields?).
- Docs: ORCHESTRATION.md 16.10 (and the header, 16.6, 16.7), DEVELOPMENT.md 13.
Design points interpreted rather than followed (flag to the reviewer / orchestrator):
1. CheckOptions.metrics (an injectable exit) is added. The design says metrics.ts injects the writer but gives CheckOptions no field for it.
2. A deferral text without a ticket differs from the gate's in three places, not two: the Deferred-as-ticket sentence, the harness-message sentence, and the exception drops the /rules let q-N half (there is no ticket id). The spec pins all three.
3. CheckResult.rules[].effect is Effect or script (design: Effect): a script rule whose script was refused and whose failure setting lets the call through has no effect of its own. rules lists every rule that matched the event and filter, in id order (person rules, then code entries), with the value of its condition. scripts lists refused scripts with outcome refused; the design's outcome union is kept, only refused is produced.
4. The Right path of a block is generic (Do not repeat the call. Continue with other planned work, or tell the human what you need and why.) because rules carry no right-path field; the Boundary names the rule id, title, who set it, when and for how long, and the condition as a statement.
5. Detectors: no host reports detector liveness yet, so a signal a detector defines reads as unknown unless a person set a value. Revisit with the detector step (blocked).
6. peakUntil needs a glm-peak value from the caller (true or false); the design only says it needs glm-peak. From a heartbeat, the end of the peak is its nextChangeAt, used only when the value is true and the change has not passed.
7. Usage-error texts, notes and subjects reasons are Chinese (the design's own strings are); the refusal text and the show text are English. show appends the notes as plain lines.
8. A directory outside git with no .llm/ is judged as having no state, with a note (design silent). The root comes from projectOf.
9. Re-read: any load plan counts as a disagreement (also a pending snapshot), so such a project waits 150 ms; the replay note is written only when the final source is a replay.
10. The design lists a propose subcommand; it is not built (blocked) and is a usage error. CheckOptions.runScript is not built either (scripts are never run).
